title: Constructible continuous modules: normalized stratified integral lattices
statement:
Fix $q=p^a$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $A$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For every separated finite-type $k$-scheme $W$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_W=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/\varpi^n)_W$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and $E_W=B_W[1/\varpi]$. Let $A_W^{\mathrm{cond}}$ and $E_W^{\mathrm{cond}}$ be the coefficient rings pulled from the condensed topological rings $A$ and $E$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Modules over these pulled rings are internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]; modules over $B_W,E_W$ are sectionwise sheaf modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

The canonical condensed-to-continuous coefficient maps of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-realizations], composed with the finite-quotient comparisons in [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization], give ring isomorphisms
$$A_W^{\mathrm{cond}}\cong B_W,\qquad E_W^{\mathrm{cond}}\cong E_W.$$
The integral map has $n$th projection exactly reduction modulo $\varpi^n$, the rational map is its localization, and the square for $A\hookrightarrow E$ commutes. These maps are natural under locally closed restriction; their successive restriction and finite coefficient-extension comparisons are the quotient, localization and balanced tensor comparisons. Under the resulting encoding [def-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-module-encoding], an internal module is lisse if and only if its encoded sectionwise module is pro-etale locally finite free. This includes rank zero and local variation of ranks. The encoding transports inverse images, submodule inclusions and ordinary scalar extensions by the identity on the underlying sheaves and module actions, and on tensor expressions its comparison sends $r\otimes m$ to $r\otimes m$ [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence].

Let $T$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, and let $F$ be a constructible $E_T$-module sheaf: on the members of some finite locally closed partition it is pro-etale locally finite free [def-constructible-stratification]. There is a finite partition $T=\coprod_\nu T_\nu$ by reduced locally closed subschemes and, at this same field $E$, lisse $B_{T_\nu}$-submodules $L_\nu\subseteq F|_{T_\nu}$, with the inclusion inducing
$$L_\nu[1/\varpi]\xrightarrow{\sim}F|_{T_\nu}.$$
Here lisse means pro-etale locally a finite direct sum of the coefficient sheaf. These are images under the displayed encoding of genuine internal integral lattice inclusions on a finite refinement of a lisse partition of $F$. Replacement of every member of that refinement by its reduced structure preserves the inclusion, lisseness and the displayed localization isomorphism. Further locally closed restriction gives the pulled-back lattice and the pulled-back localization isomorphism using these same coefficient maps. The empty partition is permitted when $T$ is empty, and rank-zero sheaves have rank-zero lattices. No global lisse lattice on $T$ is asserted.

proof.text: Choose the normalized coefficient family separately at each finite coefficient field using lem-zl-normalized-continuous-coefficient-family. These coefficient and encoding maps are determined by the section, quotient and tensor-unit normalizations; no arbitrary lattice data are chosen in a definition. Obtain CoefficientGeometry for this family using lem-zl-continuous-coefficient-geometric-coherence. Fill ordinary_scalars using lem-zl-ordinary-section-scalar-comparison and strata using lem-zl-normalized-stratified-embedded-lattices for the chosen coefficient family at that field. The Family constructor combines these independent pieces with the identical restriction, field-change and coherence fields. Its only use of l≠D.p is in the fixed-field lattice argument.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q133-4e9049896 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS, no changes; I read all seven steps and every cited statement. Shape: the branch is one commit touching only the item JSON and the report, with no new nodes. The statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to the base (sha 931b4d32), so nothing was weakened. The item is still unsplit with no reviewed record in live and side-live, so nothing supersedes it, and there is no repair note. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, there is no cycle and no SGA citation. Source: Bhatt-Scholze Def 6.8.1, Lemma 6.8.2(1)(2), Def 6.8.3, Prop 6.8.4(4)(6) and the first paragraph of Lemma 6.8.13. The core per-stratum lattice is the existing node sk-lem-stratified-lattice (same pulled condensed A and E, fixed E, ranks may vary). Stacks tags 01T5, 01T6, 03EK, 03EL, 00YV and 054M carry the labels the steps name. Step 1: Noetherian, separated, finite-type hypotheses for every stratum come from mathlib-status nodes plus elementary arguments. Step 2: nonarchimedean absolute value gives totally disconnected A and E, so the chart is an isomorphism. In the continuousCoefficientCompletion Lean statement, index n projects to coefficientExtensionIdeal(n+1), so the item's exponent n is index n-1. A^c[1/varpi] = E^c holds on Noetherian schemes, and uniqueness into the limit and out of the localization pins the maps. Step 3: chart naturality and pullback composition cover locally closed immersions with no etale assumption; in a ramified extension quotients are compared only on compatible powers. Step 4: the internal coequalizer equals the sheafified sectionwise balanced tensor (sheafification is strong monoidal), and inverse image is exact and strong monoidal. Step 5: the local-freeness lemma works for any scheme, with varying or zero ranks. Step 6: the lattice lemma plus the embedded-lattice comparison give the localization identification; inverting l or varpi gives the same result. Step 7: the reduction is a surjective closed immersion, inverse image is exact and preserves lisseness and the localization isomorphism; empty T and rank zero are handled. Edge cases checked: empty T, zero module, varying ranks, a point, nonreduced strata, ramified E', and the nodal example with no global lattice. Duplicate candidates checked and not duplicates: the continuous lisse-stratified-lattices and constructible-integral-stratum nodes, the NL topological-stratified-lisse-lattices node, the lisse-e-constructible-integral-lattice node and the rational-stratum integral-model nodes; none gives embedded lattices together with the encoding and reduction clauses. The declared tool uses are accepted: coefficient, encoding and permanence lemmas, the stratified-lattice lemma and its embedded-lattice comparison, and the absolute-value lemma, all used as black boxes below unit step 1 without replacing it. Advisory: step 7 does not write out that the scalar-extension map on pulled condensed coefficients is an isomorphism (one line from sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients and sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars(5)). The report mentions citations.json and searches.jsonl, which are sandbox files not on the branch.
